title: Final review of the Phase 2 diff
description: Review the full Phase 2 diff against the epic acceptance and SPEC §12 Phase 2, with the two operator constraints as the checklist: (a) is orchestration config and logic TRULY extracted from ticks — no execution package left behind, no unpinned read of a ticks-owned file, no ticks Go import; and (b) is the herdr executor robust to a herdr upgrade — a supported range rather than a point, capabilities read, required fields loud, the wire vocabulary pinned and diffed against the server's schema, no verdict derived from the substrate. Resolve or route findings before close-out. Verify a claimed defect against the base commit BEFORE any repair is built on it: the Phase 1 epic lost a wave to a repair built on a defect that did not exist.
notes:
2026-09-14 08:27 - Defect pass (opus, read-only) on the Phase 2 diff: 2 blockers, 7 should-fix, 5 nits. Both blockers violate the epic's OWN x6j guarantee inside the code that claims it — a launch slower than the client call timeout becomes a verdict AND tears down a live agent (verified: DefaultStartupTimeout 60s vs DefaultCallTimeout 30s), and Cancel writes a cancellation over an attempt that already reported, renaming a succeeded verdict. Routed as ticks 1eq (blockers) and etp (the seven should-fix, all the same family: an unknown answered as a fact). CRITICAL CONTEXT, verified in code: usableProfile (internal/reconcile/profiles.go:307) refuses any profile whose executor is not local-subprocess, so nothing constructs herdr.Executor outside tests. Every finding is LATENT — they are what a first real run would hit. Two guarantees confirmed genuinely held: the executor seam (the no-herdr-code check is enforced, not asserted) and durable-evidence-only collect (no client call in that path; the all-errors fixture really drives a verdict from the report alone).
2026-09-14 08:29 - Acceptance pass (opus, read-only): 3 MET, 1 PARTIAL, 2 NOT MET. NOT MET (1) the headline item — a real epic through ticfac run-epic on herdr — the executor is UNREACHABLE, not merely unexercised: dispatch.go:1390 hardcodes subprocess and profiles.go:311 refuses any other executor, with no --executor flag. NOT MET (4) the herdr protocol and server version are not fields of the pinned Provenance object; they live only on herdr's private attemptRecord, which contradicts the epic description and the 2026-09-11 split decision. PARTIAL (3) the version range is real and correct; the capability half is vacuous — RequireCapability has no callers outside the client and a test PINS that the refusal cannot arise. Routed as ticks to1 (wiring + provenance) and ic0 (capability clause, the discarded above-warn warning, the skippable drift test). On the operator's two requirements: (b) protocol robustness ACHIEVED and called the best work in the epic; (a) extraction HALF achieved — the seam is genuinely clean with no ticks Go dependency and every crossing pinned or version-gated, but nothing was removed from ticks, tk factory remains a full duplicate, and the sandbox loop is still tk. 'Extracted' currently means copied with a good boundary.
2026-09-14 15:34 - Acceptance RE-CHECK (opus, read-only, after the repairs): 5 MET, 1 PARTIAL, 0 NOT MET — both items the first pass failed are repaired and INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED, not taken from the worker's report. Item 1 (headline): the executor is genuinely reachable (internal/cli/executor.go:34-49 names both, executorFactory routes on the profile at :61-82, usableProfile at profiles.go:307-334 now asks whether the build can honour an executor rather than insisting on subprocess), and the demo repo's OWN records were checked — origin/epic/uup's checkpoint reads completed with all four ticks closed. Caveat kept: a throwaway repo whose implement ticks write one note each; no production epic has run on it. Item 4: the two substrate fields are in the PINNED Provenance (records.go:53-66) in the closed field list, in both schemas at bundle 5.2.0, and every herdr record on the demo branch carries protocol 22 / server 0.9.0. Item 3 stays PARTIAL on the capability half — now transcribed as a decision, which was the reviewer's actual complaint. Operator requirements: (b) robustness ACHIEVED, called the strongest work in the epic; (a) extraction is a real pinned dependency-free boundary with the original still live, so 'extracted' means 'copied'. Two things fixed on the spot: internal/ was not gofmt-clean (CI excludes only ^contracts/, so it could fail the PR gate alone), and the capability amendment existed only in a doc comment. Eleven residuals for the close-out; the pin-on-unmerged-branches one is filed as tick 3ku.
